changelog.title: What changed in Noeis
changelog.standfirst: A short issue whenever the app changes in a way you would notice. Written by a person, dated, and never longer than it needs to be.

issues.headline: No unread counts. Ever.
paragraphs: The newsstand used to tie a little ribbon across each cover saying "5 new". It also covered the date. Both were mistakes, and both are gone: a paper with something you have not read now says New, ahead of its date, and never how many.
This is now a rule the app cannot break. A test fails the build if anyone writes a number in front of "new" or "unread". The [manifesto](/manifesto) says why.
Also: finishing a book prints its colophon, the reading line learned three commands it will not tell you about, and after midnight the rooms dim. Go find them.

issues.headline: Work hangs its dates in the margin
paragraphs: Dates in Work notes, This week and the project log now hang in the left margin, the way a diarist writes them. The writing gets the column to itself.
Agents write in pencil now, everywhere. What Claude Code or Codex leaves you stays marked as theirs until you ink it, and you can strike it with a reason they will read next time.

issues.headline: Plainer words
paragraphs: We went through every sentence in the app and took out the ones that sounded like a database talking. Receipt, durable, provenance and metadata are now banned by a test, the way they should have been from the start.
The CLI learned to search, read, save and note from any shell, and to connect itself to Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code without you opening a config file.

issues.headline: Think opens on a desk
paragraphs: Think now opens on what you were writing, with Working, Ideas and Closed down the side. Closing a piece asks what it became, which turns out to be the only question that matters.
Work got a hill: where each project stands, uphill while you are still figuring it out, downhill once you know what to do.

manifesto.kicker: A rule you can't turn off
manifesto.title: No unread counts, anywhere, ever
manifesto.standfirst: Noeis will tell you that something is new. It will never tell you how much.
paragraphs: Every reading app eventually grows a number. It starts small, a little 3 beside a feed, and it is meant kindly. Within a month it is 214, and the app has stopped being a place you read and become a place you owe.

A number in front of the word unread is a debt. Debts get paid off, quickly and without pleasure, or they get declared bankrupt with Mark all as read. Neither is reading. Both are why most people stop opening the app that was supposed to make them smarter.

Reading that compounds works the other way. You read the one thing that matters tonight and let the rest wait. What waits is not behind; it is on the nightstand. When a paper has something you have not seen, Noeis says so, by name: Something new in This Week in AI. That is information. 23 new is pressure.

So this is a rule, and it is written into the app itself: a test fails the build if anyone, including us, puts a number in front of new or unread. There is no setting for it, because a setting would mean we were not sure.
Counts of what you made are fine. Forty-one lines in a book, six questions still open, twenty-three sittings: those are yours, and they add up. Only the counts of what you have not done yet are gone.
